title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 2.84
exact_target: Is there an irrational unit-modulus quadratic parameter for which the critical orbit is dense in the entire Julia set?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
For $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$, let
$P_\lambda(z)=\lambda(z+z^2)$. Assume $\lambda$ is not a root of unity, equivalently $\lambda=e^{2\pi i\alpha}$ for some irrational real $\alpha$. The point zero is an irrationally indifferent fixed point. The unique finite critical point is $c=-1/2$, because $P_\lambda'(z)=\lambda(1+2z)$.
Let $J(P_\lambda)$ be the Julia set, defined as the complement in the sphere of the open set where the iterates $\{P_\lambda^n:n\ge0\}$ are normal in the spherical metric. Does there exist such a parameter $\lambda$ for which the positive critical orbit is dense in that Julia set?
\[
\overline{\{P_\lambda^n(-1/2):n\ge1\}}=J(P_\lambda).
\]
The closure is in the complex plane, or equivalently in the sphere since a polynomial Julia set is compact and bounded. The assertion asks for one suitable irrational unit-modulus parameter, not for every such parameter. Merely accumulating on part of the Julia set, or having a dense orbit for some point other than the critical point, is insufficient. No assumption of linearizability at zero is added to the parameter requirement.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Is there an irrational unit-modulus quadratic parameter for which the critical orbit is dense in the entire Julia set?
